rationale: The representative boundary error strongly favors punctuation after a coordinated subject noun phrase, although the batch documents show paragraph breaks after forms such as “Lily and the scissors” and “Tom and the small scissors/needles.” Add a compact suffix rule for a proper noun, conjunction, determiner, optional adjective, and noun to support a paragraph break without encoding any particular name or story. The prior structural candidate was rejected in favor of the weight-only update because its complexity increased and its current-batch loss was worse; this narrower rule addresses a concrete repeated boundary pattern. It could also raise paragraph-break probability after similar coordinated noun phrases in contexts where another continuation is valid, so the replay gate should decide whether the generalization is acceptable. The free-generation sample is diagnostic only and is not treated as training evidence.
